s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of severe upper abdominal pain with associated nausea and vomiting, worsened by oral intake, in a post-surgical patient
salient_findings: Sudden-onset, sharp upper abdominal pain rated 9/10
Pain worsened with oral intake
Associated nausea and vomiting
Generalized abdominal tenderness, most pronounced in the right hypochondrium
Abnormal contrast-enhanced abdominal CT findings with a cluster of small-bowel loops and spiral pattern of central mesenteric vessels
key_facts: 36-year-old woman presented with acute abdominal pain
Pain awakened her early in the morning
Pain was minimally relieved by oxycodone
Patient had undergone Roux-en-Y gastric bypass three weeks earlier
Patient had intermittent nausea after surgery
Patient denied bloating, changes in bowel habits, or urinary symptoms
Medical history included type 2 diabetes mellitus
Patient was taking pantoprazole, metformin, and semaglutide
Patient had undergone multiple abdominal surgeries
Vital signs were within normal limits
Laboratory studies showed normal hemoglobin, slightly elevated white-cell count, and normal liver function tests
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed a cluster of small-bowel loops and spiral pattern of central mesenteric vessels
